newsitem.title: USA: Enron says rate timetable upto OPUC.
newsitem.headline: Enron says rate timetable upto OPUC.

text.p: Enron Corp said that the timescale for the implementation of $141 million in rate cuts resulting from the proposed merger of Enron and Portland General Corp for Oregon electricity consumers is up to the state's industry regulator.
"The Oregon Public Utilities Commission will decide on the timescale, we understand they initially wanted a four year schedule," Ken Lay, chairman of Enron told a conference call.
Enron and Portland General increased an offer of $106 million to the OPUC to $141 million after the staff of the Oregon regulator rejected their savings offers as inadequate.
The companies said they would deliver their revised formal offer to the OPUC within 24 hours.
Asked whether he expected redundancies as a result of the merger, Lay said there would not be largescale layoffs.
"This is not a merger about layoffs. We do not have overlapping businesses," Lay said. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
